AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What word describes manure made from once-living things? (1 mark)
   A. Organic
   B. Mineral only
   C. Metal
   D. Plastic

2. Which is a benefit of compost to sandy soil? (1 mark)
   A. It removes all nutrients
   B. It helps the soil to hold water
   C. It makes the soil disappear
   D. It makes the soil more sandy

3. Which is a benefit of using less fuel? (1 mark)
   A. More smoke is made
   B. The family saves money
   C. More trees must be cut
   D. The family spends more

4. Which is a problem of cutting many trees for firewood? (1 mark)
   A. Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   B. More rain falls at once
   C. Trees grow faster
   D. The soil becomes richer

5. Which of these can be used to keep boiled water hot? (1 mark)
   A. An open basin
   B. A thermos flask
   C. A metal spoon
   D. A hot stone

6. Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire? (1 mark)
   A. To use more wood
   B. So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   C. To make the food colder
   D. To cook faster than a cooker

7. Why are tins with pebbles tied on a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. They make it heavy
   B. They feed birds
   C. They store water
   D. They make noise and flash to frighten animals

8. Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds? (1 mark)
   A. Ripening millet
   B. Compost
   C. Firewood
   D. Rocks

9. Which is a way of conserving wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Selling them
   B. Protecting their homes such as forests
   C. Setting fires in the bush
   D. Cutting down all trees

10. Why is it wrong to kill every bird that visits a field? (1 mark)
   A. Birds cannot eat crops
   B. Birds are always good
   C. Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   D. Birds pay tax

11. Which crop can be harvested about four to six weeks after sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Millet
   B. Mango
   C. Radish
   D. Banana

12. Why do some farmers tie a young tree to a stake? (1 mark)
   A. To stop it growing
   B. To keep it upright in wind
   C. To feed it
   D. To make it thicker

13. How far should mulch be from the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Piled tightly against it
   B. Ten metres
   C. Not needed
   D. A small gap away

14. Why should fruit be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dry
   B. To remove dirt and germs
   C. To make it sour
   D. To change its colour

15. What do flowers become in a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Roots
   B. Fruits
   C. Soil
   D. Trunks

16. What do leaves do for a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Take in water from the soil
   B. Hold the tree in the ground
   C. Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   D. Make the trunk

17. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A plant grown in water
   B. A seed in a bag
   C. A dead plant
   D. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree

18. Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Fewer vitamins
   B. Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   C. More expenses
   D. Less food

19. What is the young one of a goat called? (1 mark)
   A. Calf
   B. Chick
   C. Kid
   D. Lamb

20. Which of these is an energy-giving food? (1 mark)
   A. Orange
   B. Ugali
   C. Spinach
   D. Fish

21. Which of these animal foods is rich in protein? (1 mark)
   A. Cassava
   B. Bread
   C. Fish
   D. Banana

22. Which of these is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Cooking oil
   C. Ugali
   D. Sukuma wiki

23. Why should we not skip breakfast? (1 mark)
   A. It makes you tired
   B. Breakfast is a waste of money
   C. It is not real food
   D. The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day

24. Which of these is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A frying pan
   B. A cup
   C. A bucket
   D. A bowl

25. Which of these foods needs a long time of boiling before it is soft enough to eat? (1 mark)
   A. Ripe banana
   B. Tomato
   C. Cucumber
   D. Dry beans

26. What is boiling? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking without heat
   B. Cooking in the sun
   C. Cooking in a little oil
   D. Cooking food in bubbling hot water

27. Why do we crack an egg into a bowl first? (1 mark)
   A. To cook it
   B. To make it hot
   C. To make it grow
   D. To check it and remove bits of shell

28. Why should food be dry before it is put into hot oil? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes hot oil splash
   B. Water makes oil colourless
   C. Water makes food sweet
   D. Water makes oil cold

29. Why do farmers and cleaners wear personal protective equipment? (1 mark)
   A. To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   B. To look tall
   C. To keep food hot
   D. To make work slower

30. Which PPE would you wear on your hands to handle dirty things? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gloves
   C. Gumboots
   D. Headgear

31. Why should you bathe every day? (1 mark)
   A. To make skin dry
   B. To make the body hot
   C. To waste water
   D. To remove sweat, dirt and germs

32. Which method removes dry dirt from the floor with a broom? (1 mark)
   A. Washing
   B. Dusting
   C. Sweeping
   D. Mopping

33. In which direction do you sweep a room? (1 mark)
   A. From the corners towards the middle or door
   B. Only the middle
   C. Only along the walls
   D. Randomly

34. Why should dusters and mops be washed after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. So they wear out
   C. So they do not spread dirt and germs
   D. To make them smell

35. What is the use of labelling PPE? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To make it heavier
   C. To tear it
   D. So each item goes back to its owner

36. How much of each edge is folded twice for the handkerchief hem? (1 mark)
   A. About 1 cm each time
   B. 10 cm
   C. 1 mm
   D. 20 cm

37. Which thread colour is best for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. One that shows clearly on the cloth
   B. One matching the cloth exactly
   C. White on white
   D. Black on black

38. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With scissors
   B. By pulling the thread out
   C. With a very big knot
   D. With a small back stitch

39. In long and short tacking, the pattern is (1 mark)
   A. No stitch
   B. All gaps long
   C. A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   D. All stitches short

40. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. Under your foot
   B. In your teeth
   C. Above your head
   D. In the left hand while sewing with the right

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

42. Give two reasons why goats are suitable for dry areas. (2 marks)

43. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)

44. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)

45. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)

46. Describe how to build a compost heap using layers. (4 marks)

47. How can a family get a balanced meal cheaply? (2 marks)

48. Explain what is meant by direct sowing. (2 marks)

49. Name three foods that are boiled. (3 marks)

50. Explain how to sow tiny seeds in a drill. (4 marks)

51. Explain what is meant by a balanced meal. (2 marks)

52. Name four fuels used for cooking in homes. (2 marks)

53. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)

54. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

55. Explain the steps for dusting a room. (4 marks)

56. Why must fish be dried before shallow frying? (3 marks)

57. Explain how measuring skills help you in tacking. (3 marks)

58. Describe how to prepare a planting hole for a fruit tree. (4 marks)

59. Give two advantages of direct sowing. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #18 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Organic
   Organic means it comes from plants and animals.

2. B — It helps the soil to hold water
   Compost holds water like a sponge.

3. B — The family saves money
   Buying less fuel means spending less.

4. A — Forests shrink and soil can be washed away
   Trees protect soil and water, so cutting them harms the environment.

5. B — A thermos flask
   A flask keeps water hot so it need not be boiled again.

6. B — So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   Fuel is not wasted waiting.

7. D — They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   Noise and movement scare animals.

8. A — Ripening millet
   Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

9. B — Protecting their homes such as forests
   Protecting habitats lets animals live.

10. C — Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   Wild animals are needed for balance in nature.

11. C — Radish
   Radish grows very quickly.

12. B — To keep it upright in wind
   Stakes protect against bending.

13. D — A small gap away
   Mulch touching the stem can cause rot.

14. B — To remove dirt and germs
   Clean fruit is safe to eat.

15. B — Fruits
   Fruits develop from flowers.

16. C — Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   Leaves make food using sunlight.

17. D — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

18. B — Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   Growing at home saves money.

19. C — Kid
   A young goat is a kid.

20. B — Ugali
   Ugali is a starchy staple.

21. C — Fish
   Fish is a protein food.

22. D — Sukuma wiki
   Vegetables give vitamins and minerals.

23. D — The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   Breakfast gives energy for school.

24. A — A frying pan
   A flat pan holds a little oil.

25. D — Dry beans
   Dry beans are hard and need long cooking.

26. D — Cooking food in bubbling hot water
   Boiling uses hot water.

27. D — To check it and remove bits of shell
   You avoid a bad egg spoiling the pan.

28. A — Water makes hot oil splash
   Splashing oil can burn.

29. A — To protect the body from dirt, injury and germs
   PPE is clothing and gear that protects us from harm.

30. B — Gloves
   Gloves cover the hands.

31. D — To remove sweat, dirt and germs
   Bathing keeps the body clean.

32. C — Sweeping
   Sweeping uses a broom.

33. A — From the corners towards the middle or door
   This gathers dirt in one place.

34. C — So they do not spread dirt and germs
   Dirty tools spread dirt.

35. D — So each item goes back to its owner
   Labels avoid mix-ups.

36. A — About 1 cm each time
   The raw edge is hidden.

37. A — One that shows clearly on the cloth
   It is easy to see and pull out.

38. D — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

39. C — A long stitch followed by a short stitch
   The pattern alternates.

40. D — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: They eat leaves, shrubs and grass, and can live where cattle find little to eat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.

45. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a shady place; lay sticks; add a dry layer, a green layer and dung; sprinkle soil and water; repeat to chest height; cover the heap.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for place, base and layers, soil and water, and covering.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Grow vegetables and fruits at home and use cheap proteins such as beans, omena or eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Sowing seeds straight into the place where the crop will grow until harvest.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sowing seeds where the crop stays, 1 mark for no transplanting.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes, eggs, cassava, maize, beans, rice (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a shallow drill about 1 cm deep; mix seeds with sand; sprinkle thinly in the drill; cover lightly with fine soil; water gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A meal that has foods from all the main food groups in the right amounts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for foods from all groups, 1 mark for right amounts.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Firewood, charcoal, gas and kerosene.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each fuel, total 2.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Open windows; use a slightly damp clean cloth; dust from high to low; shake and wash the duster outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wet food makes the hot oil splash, which can burn people, so the fish should be dried with a cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for splash, 1 for burns, 1 for drying.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Measuring gives correct stitch lengths, straight lines and correct size of the item.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a sunny site; dig a hole about half a metre wide and deep; put topsoil aside; mix topsoil with compost; put some mixture back in the hole.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Roots are not disturbed, no nursery is needed, saves time and work (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.
